emailConfig.useCaseFormDesc: Set your form plugin (Contact Form 7, WPForms, Gravity Forms, Elementor, etc.) to notify by email, and forward those notifications to your agent's address. teamSales.name: Sales
teamSales.short: Answers every lead in seconds, qualifies and books.
teamSales.lead: When a customer writes to you, on any channel, the agent answers, advises them with your catalog, asks the qualifying questions and logs them in your CRM. By the time your salesperson steps in, the customer has already said what they want.
teamSales.label: Sales assistant

chat.m1: I'm looking for a voltage regulator.
chat.m2: I want to be upfront: we don't sell that equipment on its own. Tell me what problem you want to solve and I'll guide you.

teamSales.storyH: What the agent does with every customer who writes to you
teamSales.storyLead: Today a customer writes and waits. When someone answers, they have to ask the basics, look the person up in the CRM and copy the details by hand. The agent does all of that before your salesperson steps in, always in the same order.
teamSales.methodClose: Up to here the agent leaves the sale prepared. Who closes it is up to you: your salesperson, or the agent itself if you set it up to close.

s1.title: Answers and opens the conversation
s1.text: It answers right away and asks what the customer is looking for. With your catalog and documents at hand, it guides them and says clearly what you do offer.
s1.result: A customer attended from the first message

s2.title: Finds out what they need
s2.text: It asks open questions, one at a time: their situation, what is urgent, the size of their business and what they use today. You define what it must ask before passing the case on.
s2.result: A concrete need, not an “I want information”

s3.title: Explains how you solve it
s3.text: With what the customer shared, it explains how your product or service solves their case. It talks about benefits and doesn't promise more than you offer.
s3.result: A customer who understands why your offer fits

s4.title: Asks for details without sounding like a form
s4.text: Name and email first, then phone and company. It asks about budget last, once there is trust. Everything is saved in your CRM.
s4.result: A complete contact, with nobody typing it in

s5.title: Qualifies and sets the next step
s5.text: It gives the customer an interest score from 0 to 10 and places them in your pipeline. If interest is high, it proposes a call or a demo with your team, and with the GenSmart agenda it books it in the same conversation. If it is low, it offers resources by email.
s5.result: Your salesperson sees who to call first and opens the full conversation

control.title: You define how far the agent goes
control.lead: What the agent does with a customer who wants to buy is set in its instructions and in the tools you connect. You set the rules.

r1.title: Negotiate
r1.text: You tell it what it can offer and up to what discount. Anything above that cap, it hands to your salesperson.

r2.title: Quote
r2.text: With your prices loaded or by querying your system through API, it builds the quote under the rules you define.

r3.title: Close
r3.text: With your store or API connected, it creates the order in the same conversation. Without a connection, it leaves the close to your salesperson.

r4.title: Hand over to a person
r4.text: You decide when: a bigger discount, a large quote or a customer who asks to talk to someone. They get the full conversation.

q1.question: Who closes the sale?
q1.answer: You define it. Your salesperson can close using the conversation and the data the agent left, or you can set the agent up to close. You can take over the conversation at any time.

q2.question: What if they ask for something I don't sell?
q2.answer: The agent says so clearly and suggests what you do offer, using the catalog you loaded.

q3.question: Can it ask technical questions?
q3.answer: You define what it must ask before passing the request, such as application, power or city.

q4.question: How does the request reach my team?
q4.answer: As a contact and opportunity in your CRM, with the conversation and the data it captured.

q5.question: Can I step into the conversation?
q5.answer: Yes. You take control whenever you want and the full history stays in view.

teamCustomerSupport.name: Customer support
teamCustomerSupport.short: Resolves repeated questions and leaves the cases that matter to your team.
teamCustomerSupport.lead: When a customer writes with a question or a problem, on any channel, the agent answers with your business information and guides them until it is solved. If the case needs a person, it passes it to your team with the summary already written.
teamCustomerSupport.label: Support assistant

chat.m2: It shipped yesterday and arrives tomorrow before 6 pm. Here is the tracking link.

teamCustomerSupport.storyH: What the agent does with every customer who needs help
teamCustomerSupport.storyLead: Today your team answers the same questions all day. Meanwhile, the customer with a serious problem waits behind those who only wanted a detail. The agent solves the simple ones and passes to your team only the cases that require a person.
teamCustomerSupport.methodClose: The repetitive solves itself. What calls for judgment reaches your team with the full context.

s1.title: Welcomes the customer
s1.text: It greets them warmly, introduces itself as a support assistant and asks how it can help.
s1.result: A customer attended without waiting in line

s2.title: Understands the problem
s2.text: If information is missing, it asks clarifying questions before answering.
s2.result: A clear problem, not a loose complaint

s3.title: Looks for the answer in your information
s3.text: It checks your knowledge base, with the documents, policies and links you loaded. If it can't find the answer, it says so and doesn't make one up.
s3.result: Answers based on what you said

s4.title: Guides until it is solved
s4.text: It gives the solution step by step. For a technical problem, it walks them through the diagnosis one step at a time. It acknowledges the customer's frustration and, before closing, confirms they are satisfied.
s4.result: A customer who solves their problem without waiting for anyone

s5.title: Passes the case to a person
s5.text: If it can't solve it in two attempts or the customer asks to talk to someone, it sends a button to open the conversation with your team and leaves the case summary. It doesn't promise refunds or credits: it explains that a person will review the case.
s5.result: Your team gets the case summarized and the customer repeats nothing

teamOperationsBooking.name: Operations and bookings
teamOperationsBooking.short: Fill your calendar without anyone answering: the agent books the appointment in the conversation.
teamOperationsBooking.lead: When a customer writes to ask for an appointment, the agent checks your calendar, offers open slots and leaves the booking confirmed in the same conversation. Your front desk no longer chases times or types in data.
teamOperationsBooking.label: Booking agent

chat.m1: I'd like an appointment Thursday at 10.
chat.m2: That time is taken. I have 11:30 or 15:00 open. Which do you prefer?

teamOperationsBooking.storyH: What the agent does with every customer who wants an appointment
teamOperationsBooking.storyLead: Today booking is a back and forth of messages: the customer suggests a time, someone checks the calendar, the time is gone and it starts over. Sometimes nobody answers in time and the customer goes elsewhere. The agent closes that back and forth in a single conversation.
teamOperationsBooking.methodClose: Your team books nothing by hand. And 30 minutes before each appointment, GenSmart sends them a notice inside the platform.

s1.title: Welcomes the customer and asks what they need
s1.text: It greets them and asks which service or type of appointment they want. If they are unsure, it briefly describes what you offer so they can decide.
s1.result: A clear service from the first message

s2.title: Collects the booking details
s2.text: It asks for full name, email, phone and any preferences that matter in your business, such as the professional or the location. Then it asks which day and time suit them.
s2.result: A booking with all the details, no phone call

s3.title: Checks your calendar right then
s3.text: It checks the real availability of your calendar, with your working days and hours, the length of each appointment and the buffer between them. If the requested time is taken, it instantly offers the two or three closest ones.
s3.result: An open slot chosen by the customer, not by your front desk

s4.title: Confirms before booking
s4.text: It repeats the service, date, time and contact details and asks if everything is right. It only books once the customer says yes.
s4.result: No appointments with the wrong details

s5.title: Books and notifies both sides
s5.text: It puts the appointment in your GenSmart calendar. If the customer left their email, they get a confirmation with the date, the time and a link to add it to their Google Calendar. You get an email notice.
s5.result: A confirmed appointment nobody had to schedule

control.title: You define how far the agent goes
control.lead: The agent books within the rules of your calendar and its instructions. You set the rules.

r1.title: When people can book
r1.text: You set your working days and hours, the length of each appointment, the buffer between them and how many days ahead people can book. The agent offers nothing outside that.

r2.title: What details it asks for
r2.text: Besides name, email and phone, you tell it what matters in your business: the professional, the location or the reason for the visit.

r3.title: Cancel and reschedule
r3.text: By default the agent books, but does not move or cancel appointments. You make those changes from the calendar. If your system allows it, you can connect it through API.

r4.title: When it hands over to a person
r4.text: You decide when: a special case or a customer who asks to talk to someone. On WhatsApp, web and Facebook they get a button and your team sees the full conversation.

control.lead: What the agent says and offers about a payment is set in its instructions and in the tools you connect. You set the rules.

r1.title: Where it gets the balance
r1.text: From the documents you load or, if you connect your system through API, from each customer's real balance. If it does not have the figure, it does not make it up and hands the conversation to a person.

r2.title: How people pay
r2.text: You define the payment methods it shares: bank transfer, card or your payment link. If your payments platform has an API, it can generate the link for each invoice.

r3.title: What it can offer and how it speaks
r3.text: You set the tone and the terms: whether it can offer installments, until when, under what rules. Anything outside that it does not improvise. Check the collections regulations that apply to you before defining them.

r4.title: When it hands over to a person
r4.text: You decide when: a disputed amount, a payment plan or a customer who describes a hard situation. On WhatsApp, web and Facebook they get a button and your team sees the full conversation.

console.name: Andrés
console.summary: Asked about the September invoice balance ($320,000). Requested the payment link and committed to pay on Friday.
console.m1: How much do I owe on the September invoice?
console.m2: It is $320,000, due on September 30. Would you rather pay by bank transfer or with a payment link?
console.m3: With the link, please. I can pay on Friday.
console.m4: Done, Andrés. I am sending you the link and noting your payment for Friday.

q1.question: Does the agent write to my customers first to collect?
q1.answer: No. The agent replies when the customer writes. On WhatsApp, it can also only reply within 24 hours of the customer's last message.

q2.question: How does it know how much each customer owes?
q2.answer: From the documents you load or by looking up your system through API when you connect it. If it does not have the figure, it does not make it up and hands the conversation to a person.

q3.question: What happens if the customer disagrees with the amount?
q3.answer: The agent does not argue. It hands the full conversation to your team so a person can resolve it.

q4.question: How does it send the payment link?
q4.answer: It shares the link or payment details you define. If your payments platform has an API, it can generate the link for each invoice.

q5.question: Can I set the tone and the rules?
q5.answer: Yes. You define how it speaks, what it can offer and when it hands over to a person. Check the collections regulations that apply to you before setting your terms.
